correctness.rationale: For every integer k>=3 a symmetry average preserves feasibility and cannot raise the centered spectral norm. The radial and contrast Laplacian blocks are derived explicitly. An exact positive contrast eigenvector of eigenvalue gamma yields a universal Rayleigh upper bound on the Laplacian gap and equality conditions forcing x=1/k,y=(2-gamma)/3,z=(1+gamma)/3 among invariant matrices. The candidate satisfies every nonnegativity constraint; an exact radial characteristic factorization and the positive evaluation q(2-gamma)=(2-gamma)(3k-8)/(9k) exclude a larger negative-end SLEM. Source code reproduces five symbolic identities and independent grounded spectra; finite experiments are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2007/2009 graph-symmetry FMMC framework does not provide the k-arm length-three radical solution. The 2010 symmetric-star optimum pertains to signed-diagonal consensus: its hub holding probability (2-k)/(k+2) is strictly negative for k>=3, violating the current feasible set. The 2020 FMRMC symmetric-star formula is conditional on k*pi1<=2*pi0, false under uniform mass for k>=3; its unconditional exact classification concerns depth two. The closest indexed fixed-weight spider result bounds mixing but does not solve transition-probability optimization. These implication comparisons support a distinct claim; a residual possibility of an unindexed or overlooked equivalent result remains.

value.rationale: On a natural, infinite three-edge-arm tree family the nonnegative Markov constraint invalidates the earlier same-topology fast consensus weights. The theorem provides exact globally optimal transition probabilities, a radical spectral-gap law, a distinguished saturating hub budget, and a strict negative-spectrum certificate for all k>=3. It is a motivated complete parameter classification useful as a benchmark for spectral Markov design, not a mere numerical restatement.
